title: Brush from the crown outward
body: For 360 waves you brush in every direction, always starting at the crown and working outward. Thirty minutes a day beats two hours once a week. Use the hard brush while wolfing and the medium brush for daily training.

title: Never brush bone dry
body: Dry hair breaks and a dry scalp flakes. Work a little oil or pomade through before you brush so the bristles glide and your pattern stays hydrated.

title: Double compression = deeper waves
body: After brushing, put on your durag and then a wave cap over it. Sleeping in double compression every night is what trains the pattern to stay down.

title: Wash once a week, gently
body: Use a wave-friendly shampoo and conditioner once a week. Brush lightly in the shower with conditioner in, then rinse and moisturize straight away.

title: Wolfing: patience is the plan
body: Don't cut for four to six weeks. Keep brushing and wearing your durag, then get a low cut. Waves get deeper with every wolf cycle, so don't rush the process.

title: Finish with the soft brush
body: A few minutes with the soft brush after your pomade sets polishes the hair and brings out the shine. It is the last step before the durag goes on.
